questions.question: What changes is an NBFC-P2P required to communicate to the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.answer: An NBFC-P2P must communicate changes in address, directors, auditors, and similar matters as specified in the referenced directions.
questions.evidence: Every NBFC-P2P shall communicate change of address, directors, auditors, etc., as prescribed in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Miscellaneous) Directions, 2025.

questions.question: Which RBI directions prescribe the procedure for an NBFC-P2P to communicate changes in its address, directors, or auditors?
questions.answer: The procedure is prescribed in paragraphs 6 and 7 of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Miscellaneous) Directions, 2025.
questions.evidence: Every NBFC-P2P shall communicate change of address, directors, auditors, etc., as prescribed in paragraphs 6 and 7 of Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Miscellaneous) Directions, 2025.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific time limit within which an NBFC-P2P must notify the RBI of a change in its statutory auditors?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any deadline or time period for communicating such changes; it only references the Miscellaneous Directions for the procedure.

questions.question: How must a commercial bank obtain regulatory approval for assigning additional roles or responsibilities to its Managing Director & CEO or Chief Executive Officer?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must submit the request for regulatory approval through the Pravaah Portal at https://pravaah.rbi.org.in, as required under Section 10B(8) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
questions.evidence: A bank shall obtain regulatory approval regarding Additional Roles or Responsibilities of MD&CEO / CEO in terms of Section 10B(8) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, through the Pravaah Portal ( https://pravaah.rbi.org.in).

questions.question: Which legal provision mandates that a commercial bank seek regulatory approval before giving extra duties to its MD&CEO or CEO?
questions.answer: Section 10B(8) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 requires a commercial bank to obtain regulatory approval for additional roles or responsibilities of the MD&CEO or CEO.
questions.evidence: A bank shall obtain regulatory approval regarding Additional Roles or Responsibilities of MD&CEO / CEO in terms of Section 10B(8) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, through the Pravaah Portal ( https://pravaah.rbi.org.in).

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of additional roles that the RBI permits an MD&CEO or CEO of a commercial bank to hold concurrently?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only states that regulatory approval is required via the Pravaah Portal under Section 10B(8); it does not specify any limit on the number of additional roles.

questions.question: What loan-to-value ratio must an NBFC with an asset size of ₹100 crore or more maintain when lending against listed shares, and how quickly must any shortfall be corrected?
questions.answer: The NBFC must maintain a 50 percent LTV ratio at all times, and any shortfall due to share price movements must be made good within seven working days.
questions.evidence: maintain a LTV ratio of 50 per cent for loans granted against the collateral of shares. LTV ratio of 50 per cent is required to be maintained at all times. Any shortfall in the maintenance of the 50 percent LTV occurring on account of movement in the share prices shall be made good within seven working days.

questions.question: When an NBFC with assets of ₹100 crore or above lends more than ₹5 lakh for investment in capital markets, what type of securities must it accept as collateral?
questions.answer: It must accept only Group 1 securities as specified in the SEBI circular SMD/Policy/Cir-9/2003 dated March 11, 2003, as amended from time to time, subject to review by the Reserve Bank.
questions.evidence: in case where lending is being done for investment in capital markets, accept only Group 1 securities (specified in SMD/ Policy/ Cir - 9/ 2003 dated March 11, 2003 issued by SEBI as amended from time to time) as collateral for loans of value more than ₹5 lakh, subject to review by the Reserve Bank.

unanswerable.question: What is the penalty or supervisory action if an NBFC fails to report pledged share information to stock exchanges within the quarterly deadline?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph mandates quarterly online reporting to stock exchanges in the Annex-III format but does not specify any penalty, consequence, or supervisory action for non-compliance or late reporting.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at an NBFC that belongs to a group, am I required to implement group-wide anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing programmes?
questions.answer: Yes, every NBFC that is part of a group must implement group-wide programmes against money laundering and terror financing.
questions.evidence: every NBFC which is part of a group, shall implement group-wide programmes against money laundering and terror financing

questions.question: What safeguards must an NBFC's group-wide AML/CFT programme include regarding information shared within the group?
questions.answer: The programme must include adequate safeguards on the confidentiality and use of information exchanged, including safeguards to prevent tipping-off.
questions.evidence: such programmes shall include adequate safeguards on the confidentiality and use of information exchanged, including safeguards to prevent tipping-off

unanswerable.question: What is the deadline for NBFCs to implement these group-wide policies after the Directions come into effect?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any implementation timeline or deadline for NBFCs to adopt the group-wide policies.

questions.question: As an NBFC, must we finish a fraud investigation before we transfer a loan account to another lender or to an Asset Reconstruction Company?
questions.answer: Yes, the Applicable NBFC is required to complete the investigation from a fraud angle before transferring the loan account or credit facility to other lenders or ARCs.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC shall complete the investigation from fraud angle before transferring the loan account / credit facility to other lenders / Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs).

questions.question: If our NBFC sells a fraud-classified account to an ARC, do we still have to keep reporting updates to the RBI?
questions.answer: Yes, the NBFC must continue to report subsequent developments to the RBI by periodically obtaining the necessary information from the ARC.
questions.evidence: In cases where accounts are sold to ARCs, the Applicable NBFC shall continue to report subsequent developments in such accounts to RBI, by obtaining requisite information periodically from the concerned ARCs.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days an NBFC has to complete the fraud investigation before it may transfer the account?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the investigation to be completed before transfer but does not specify any time limit or deadline for that investigation.

questions.question: Can an NBFC hold pooled accounts managed by professional intermediaries for entities such as mutual funds or pension funds?
questions.answer: Yes, the NBFC has the option to hold pooled accounts managed by professional intermediaries on behalf of entities like mutual funds, pension funds, or other types of funds.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall have option to hold 'pooled' accounts managed by professional intermediaries on behalf of entities like mutual funds, pension funds or other types of funds.

questions.question: When may an NBFC rely on the customer due diligence performed by a professional intermediary?
questions.answer: An NBFC may rely on the intermediary's CDD at its discretion, provided the intermediary is a regulated and supervised entity with adequate systems to comply with KYC requirements.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall, at their discretion, rely on the CDD done by an intermediary, provided that the intermediary is a regulated and supervised entity and has adequate systems in place to comply with the KYC requirements of the customers.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time period allowed for an NBFC to complete beneficial owner identification for pooled accounts opened through professional intermediaries?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires identification of beneficial owners in pooled accounts but does not specify any deadline or time limit for completing this identification.

questions.question: What interest rate must a commercial bank apply to matured deposits held by a deceased individual depositor?
questions.answer: The rate shall be as per the comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits, subject to the conditions laid down in paragraph 7 of the Directions.
questions.evidence: The rate of interest on matured deposits standing in the name of a deceased individual depositor or two or more joint depositors, where one of the depositors has died, shall be as per comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits and subject to the conditions laid down in paragraph 7 of these Directions.

questions.question: Does the interest rate rule for deceased depositors also cover matured deposits of joint depositors where one has died?
questions.answer: Yes, the same rule applies to matured deposits standing in the name of two or more joint depositors where one of the depositors has died.
questions.evidence: The rate of interest on matured deposits standing in the name of a deceased individual depositor or two or more joint depositors, where one of the depositors has died, shall be as per comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits and subject to the conditions laid down in paragraph 7 of these Directions.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific interest rate percentage that a commercial bank must pay on matured deposits of a deceased depositor?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify a numeric interest rate; it only states that the rate shall be as per the comprehensive policy on interest rate on deposits and subject to conditions in paragraph 7.

questions.question: When an NBFC identifies a loan account as fraudulent, what must happen to the borrowal accounts of other group companies that share promoters or whole-time directors?
questions.answer: Those borrowal accounts must also be examined from a fraud angle by the concerned Regulated Entities under the Fraud Risk Management Directions.
questions.evidence: the borrowal accounts of other group companies, in which one or more promoter(s) / whole-time director(s) are common, shall also be subjected to examination by Regulated Entities (REs) concerned from fraud angle under these Directions.

questions.question: Which group companies' borrowal accounts are subject to fraud-angle examination after an NBFC flags a fraud account?
questions.answer: Only group companies that have one or more promoters or whole-time directors in common with the fraudulent account holder.
questions.evidence: the borrowal accounts of other group companies, in which one or more promoter(s) / whole-time director(s) are common, shall also be subjected to examination by Regulated Entities (REs) concerned from fraud angle under these Directions.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time limit allowed for Regulated Entities to complete the fraud-angle examination of the group companies' borrowal accounts after the initial fraud identification?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any deadline, timeframe, or period within which the examination must be completed.

questions.question: Which entities are covered by the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Microfinance Institution) Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: The Directions apply to every Non-Banking Financial Company – Microfinance Institution (NBFC-MFI) registered with the Reserve Bank under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
questions.evidence: These Directions shall be applicable to every Non-Banking Financial Company – Microfinance Institution (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'NBFC-MFIs' and individually as an 'NBFC-MFI') registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).

questions.question: What registration must an NBFC-MFI hold for these Directions to apply to it?
questions.answer: It must be registered with the Reserve Bank under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
questions.evidence: These Directions shall be applicable to every Non-Banking Financial Company – Microfinance Institution (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'NBFC-MFIs' and individually as an 'NBFC-MFI') registered with the Reserve Bank under the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (Act No. 2 of 1934).

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum net owned fund requirement for an NBFC-MFI to be registered under the RBI Act, 1934?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only states that the Directions apply to NBFC-MFIs registered under the RBI Act, 1934, but does not specify any capital or net owned fund thresholds for such registration.

questions.question: When does the prescribed post-shipment interest rate stop accruing for export bills drawn in foreign currency?
questions.answer: The prescribed post-shipment interest rate ceases from the date the foreign currency amount is credited to the bank's 'Nostro' account.
questions.evidence: Although there are instructions that the prescribed post-shipment interest rate will cease from the date of credit to the 'Nostro' account

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do with an exporter's credit limit once an export bill is realised?
questions.answer: The bank must promptly restore the exporter's credit limit upon realisation of the bill and pass on the rupee credit to the customer.
questions.evidence: There is, therefore, a need to promptly restore the limit of the exporters on realisation of bills and pass on the rupee credit to the customer.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days a commercial bank may take to credit the rupee equivalent to the exporter's account after the foreign currency is credited to its Nostro account?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states banks must 'promptly restore the limit' and pass on rupee credit but does not specify a concrete time limit or deadline in days.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, how does the regulation distinguish between an internet banking channel and a mobile banking channel?
questions.answer: An internet banking channel is offered over the internet via web browsers but excludes mobile applications, while a mobile banking channel uses mobile applications, USSD, and SMS.
questions.evidence: (b) Internet Banking Channel – Digital banking channel offered by a bank to its customers for operating their accounts and accessing its services over the internet (including web browser-based applications but excluding mobile applications). (c) Mobile Banking Channel – Digital banking channel offered by a bank to its customers for operating their accounts and accessing its services using mobile applications, unstructured supplementary service data (USSD) and short message service (SMS).

questions.question: What banking services can a commercial bank provide through a view-only banking facility on its digital channels, and what is explicitly prohibited?
questions.answer: A view-only facility permits services that do not alter the customer's assets or liabilities, such as balance enquiry and statement downloads, but cannot provide loans, fund transfers, or any facility creating liability or moving funds.
questions.evidence: View Only Banking Facility – A feature of digital banking channels which only allows banking services that do not alter the asset or liability of the customer viz. balance enquiry, balance viewing, account statement download, etc. Note: Loans, funds transfers, and other such facilities, which create liability for the customer and/or involve movement of funds, cannot be provided by banks having view only facility over digital channels.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of digital banking channels a commercial bank is authorised to operate under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph defines types of digital banking channels and their features but does not specify any numerical limit on how many channels a bank may operate.

questions.question: Where must an NBFC hold the first auction for gold or silver collateral?
questions.answer: The first auction must be conducted physically in the same district where the lending branch is located.
questions.evidence: The first auction shall be conducted physically in the same district in which the lending branch is located.

questions.question: What alternatives does an NBFC have if the first auction of gold or silver collateral fails?
questions.answer: If the first auction fails, the NBFC may conduct the auction in an adjoining district or hold it online.
questions.evidence: However, in case of failure of first auction, an NBFC may conduct the auction in an adjoining district or conduct online auction.

unanswerable.question: How many days after a failed first auction must an NBFC wait before conducting the second auction?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any waiting period, deadline, or time frame for conducting a subsequent auction after the first one fails.

questions.question: What must an NBFC-AA do before transferring financial information received from a Financial Information Provider to a Financial Information User?
questions.answer: The NBFC-AA must verify the identity of the Financial Information User before proceeding with any transfer of customer information.
questions.evidence: verify the identity of the Financial Information User; and, if verified

questions.question: How must an NBFC-AA transfer customer information to a Financial Information User once the user's identity has been verified?
questions.answer: The NBFC-AA must securely transfer the information to the intended recipient in accordance with the terms of the consent artefact.
questions.evidence: securely transfer the customer's information to the intended recipient in accordance with the terms of the consent artefact.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time allowed for an NBFC-AA to complete the identity verification of a Financial Information User before transferring the financial information?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time limit, deadline, or turnaround period for the verification process.

questions.question: What documents can an NBFC accept as proof of business for a sole proprietary firm under the KYC directions?
questions.answer: An NBFC must obtain any two documents from a specified list of eight options, including registration certificates, tax returns, GST certificates, IEC, professional licenses, complete income tax returns, or utility bills.
questions.evidence: the NBFC shall also obtain any two of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof as proof of business / activity in the name of the proprietary firm: (1) Registration certificate including Udyam Registration Certificate (URC) issued by the Government. (2) Certificate / licence issued by the municipal authorities under Shop and Establishment Act

questions.question: How many documents from the prescribed list must an NBFC collect for a sole proprietary firm?
questions.answer: The NBFC must obtain any two documents from the list of eight acceptable documents as proof of business for the proprietary firm.
questions.evidence: the NBFC shall also obtain any two of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof as proof of business / activity in the name of the proprietary firm:

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum permissible age of utility bills when submitted as proof of business for a sole proprietary firm?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph lists utility bills as an acceptable document but does not specify any time limit, validity period, or maximum age for such bills.

questions.question: What disclosure requirements must an NBFC impose on a builder or developer when financing a housing project regarding the mortgagee entity?
questions.answer: The NBFC must require the builder or developer to disclose the name of the mortgagee entity in all pamphlets, brochures, on-site display boards, and newspaper or magazine advertisements for the project.
questions.evidence: The builder / developer / owner / company shall disclose in the pamphlets / brochures / display boards on-site, the name(s) of the entity to which the property is mortgaged. (2) The builder/ developer/ company shall append the information relating to mortgage while publishing advertisement of a particular scheme in newspapers/ magazines etc.

questions.question: When can an NBFC release funds to a builder or developer for a housing project under these directions?
questions.answer: Funds can only be released after the builder or developer fulfills all the stipulated disclosure requirements, including disclosing the mortgagee entity name in marketing materials and indicating they will provide NOC from the mortgagee for property sales.
questions.evidence: Further, the NBFC shall ensure compliance with the above stipulations and funds shall not be released unless the builder / developer / owner / company fulfil the above requirements.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time period an NBFC has to verify the builder's compliance with the disclosure requirements before releasing funds?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that funds shall not be released until requirements are fulfilled, but does not specify any time limit or deadline for the NBFC to complete its verification.

questions.question: What policies must a commercial bank establish for its digital banking channels under the RBI Directions?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must put in place comprehensive policies for all digital banking channels that take into account all statutory and regulatory requirements, including the management of liquidity and operational risks in a digital banking scenario.
questions.evidence: Banks shall put in place comprehensive policy(ies) for all digital banking channels keeping in account all statutory and regulatory requirements (including on management of liquidity and operational risks in digital banking scenario).

questions.question: Which specific risks must a commercial bank's digital banking policies address according to the RBI Directions?
questions.answer: The policies must address the management of liquidity risk and operational risk in the digital banking scenario.
questions.evidence: Banks shall put in place comprehensive policy(ies) for all digital banking channels keeping in account all statutory and regulatory requirements (including on management of liquidity and operational risks in digital banking scenario).

unanswerable.question: What is the deadline by which a commercial bank must have these comprehensive digital banking policies approved and implemented?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that banks shall put in place comprehensive policies but does not specify any timeline, deadline, or implementation date for doing so.

questions.question: What is the maximum annual household income for a loan to qualify as a microfinance loan for an NBFC?
questions.answer: The maximum annual household income is ₹3,00,000.
questions.evidence: Microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan given to a household having annual household income up to ₹3,00,000.

questions.question: Can an NBFC link a microfinance loan to a lien on the borrower's deposit account or hypothecate any security?
questions.answer: No, the loan must not be linked with a lien on the deposit account or backed by hypothecation of any security.
questions.evidence: Further, to ensure collateral-free nature of the microfinance loan, the loan shall not be linked with a lien on the deposit account of the borrower or backed by hypothecation of any security.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum loan amount an NBFC can disburse as a microfinance loan under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph defines microfinance loans by income threshold and collateral-free nature but does not specify any maximum loan amount limit.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at an NBFC acting as a Financial Information User, what restrictions apply to how we can use or disclose financial information received through an Account Aggregator?
questions.answer: The NBFC-AA and Financial Information User must not use or disclose the financial information except as specified in the consent artefact.
questions.evidence: it shall not be used or disclosed by an NBFC-AA or the Financial Information User except as may be specified in the consent artefact.

questions.question: What document determines the permissible uses and disclosures of financial information transferred via an Account Aggregator to our NBFC as a Financial Information User?
questions.answer: The consent artefact specifies the permitted uses and disclosures of the financial information.
questions.evidence: except as may be specified in the consent artefact.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time period for which a Financial Information User may retain financial information received through an Account Aggregator before it must be deleted?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any retention period, deletion requirement, or time limit for holding financial information.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, do I need to obtain Reserve Bank approval before launching a transactional banking facility, and if so, where do I submit the application?
questions.answer: Yes, a commercial bank must obtain prior approval from the Reserve Bank of India before launching a transactional banking facility, and the application must be submitted to the Department of Regulation through the PRAVAAH portal along with the approval of the appropriate authority and supporting documents.
questions.evidence: Banks shall require prior approval of the Reserve Bank for launching transactional banking facility. Subject to fulfilment of the eligibility criteria as enumerated below, banks may apply to the Department of Regulation, Reserve Bank of India (through the PRAVAAH portal)

questions.question: If my commercial bank already had approval for mobile banking before these Directions came into effect, what must we do before launching a new digital banking channel like internet banking?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure compliance with eligibility criteria 7.1(a) to (d) — including CBS with IPv6, CRAR, minimum capital, and financial/technical capabilities — and submit a GAICA Report certified by a CERT-In empanelled auditor addressing the new channel's requirements to the Department of Regulation via PRAVAAH within 30 days of the decision to launch.
questions.evidence: If a bank had received approval for a particular digital banking channel (like mobile banking) before the date of applicability of these Directions, it shall ensure compliance to the eligibility criteria as detailed in para 7.1(a) to (d) above before launching any other digital banking channel. Further, the GAICA Report, certified by (third party) CERT-In empanelled auditor(s), addressing the specific requirement for the new proposed channels shall be sent to the Department of Regulation, Reserve Bank of India (through the PRAVAAH portal) with the approval of appropriate authority within thirty days from the decision to launch the facility.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) percentage that a commercial bank must maintain to be eligible for launching a transactional banking facility under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states compliance with the 'minimum regulatory CRAR requirement' but does not specify the actual numerical percentage, which is set elsewhere in RBI regulations.

questions.question: What obligation does a commercial bank have regarding end-use monitoring when extending rupee pre-shipment credit to exporters?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must monitor the end-use of funds, specifically the distribution of inputs by exporters to farmers for crop cultivation as per arrangements with the exporter or main processor units.
questions.evidence: The bank shall also monitor the end-use of funds, viz. distribution of the inputs by the exporters to the farmers for raising the crops as per arrangements made by the exporter / main processor units.

questions.question: What specific end-use must a commercial bank verify when providing rupee pre-shipment credit to exporters under these directions?
questions.answer: The bank must verify that inputs are distributed by exporters to farmers for raising crops according to arrangements made by the exporter or main processor units.
questions.evidence: The bank shall also monitor the end-use of funds, viz. distribution of the inputs by the exporters to the farmers for raising the crops as per arrangements made by the exporter / main processor units.

unanswerable.question: What is the required frequency or timeline for a commercial bank to conduct end-use monitoring of rupee pre-shipment credit?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states the bank shall monitor end-use but does not specify any frequency, timeline, or periodicity for such monitoring.

questions.question: What training requirements apply to call centre staff at a commercial bank that issues credit or debit cards for handling customer complaints?
questions.answer: Commercial banks issuing cards must ensure their call centre staff are adequately trained to competently handle and escalate complaints when necessary.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers shall ensure that their call centre staff are trained adequately to competently handle and escalate, a complaint, if necessary.

questions.question: Is a commercial bank that issues cards required to provide a complaint reference number even when a customer complains by phone?
questions.answer: Yes, the bank must have a system to acknowledge every complaint with a complaint or docket number for follow-up, including complaints received over the phone.
questions.evidence: There shall be a system of acknowledging customers' complaints for follow up, such as complaint number / docket number, even if the complaints are received over phone.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time allowed for a commercial bank's call centre to escalate an unresolved card complaint to a higher authority?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires automatic escalation of unresolved complaints but does not specify any time limit or deadline for such escalation.

questions.question: When is an NBFC not required to identify and verify the beneficial owners of a legal person customer?
questions.answer: An NBFC does not need to identify or verify beneficial owners when the customer or controlling interest owner is an entity listed on an Indian stock exchange, an entity resident in a notified jurisdiction listed on a stock exchange there, or a subsidiary of such listed entities.
questions.evidence: Where the customer or the owner of the controlling interest is: (i) an entity listed on a stock exchange in India, or (ii) it is an entity resident in jurisdictions notified by the Central Government and listed on stock exchanges in such jurisdictions, or (iii) it is a subsidiary of such listed entities; it is not necessary to identify and verify the identity of any shareholder or beneficial owner of such entities.

questions.question: What must an NBFC do when opening a trust, nominee, or fiduciary account for a legal person?
questions.answer: The NBFC must determine if the customer is acting on behalf of another person, obtain satisfactory evidence of the identity of the intermediaries and the persons on whose behalf they are acting, and collect details of the nature of the trust or other arrangements.
questions.evidence: In cases of trust / nominee or fiduciary accounts, the NBFC determines whether the customer is acting on behalf of another person as trustee / nominee or any other intermediary. In such cases, the NBFC shall obtain satisfactory evidence of the identity of the intermediaries and of the persons on whose behalf they are acting, as well as details of the nature of the trust or other arrangements in place.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days an NBFC has to complete beneficial owner verification after opening an account for a legal person?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time period, deadline, or maximum number of days for completing beneficial owner verification.

questions.question: Do the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025 override or replace other applicable laws and regulations for a commercial bank?
questions.answer: No, the Directions are in addition to and do not derogate from any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions currently in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

questions.question: If a commercial bank is already subject to other RBI directions or statutes, do the Governance Directions, 2025 take precedence over those existing requirements?
questions.answer: No, the Governance Directions apply alongside other laws and directions without diminishing their effect.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: Which specific statutes or regulations are considered 'other laws' that these Directions do not derogate from?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph refers generally to 'any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions' but does not enumerate or identify any specific statutes or regulations.

questions.question: What can an NBFC do in its contracts with third-party service providers to address fraud risk from wilful negligence or malpractice?
questions.answer: An NBFC may include terms and conditions in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable when their wilful negligence or malpractice is a causative factor for fraud.
questions.evidence: the Applicable NBFC may incorporate necessary terms and conditions in its agreements with third-party service providers to hold them accountable in situations where wilful negligence / malpractice by them is found to be a causative factor for fraud

questions.question: For which activities do NBFCs rely on third-party service providers that could create fraud risk?
questions.answer: NBFCs rely on third-party service providers for pre-sanction appraisal and post-sanction monitoring activities.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC places reliance on various third-party service providers as part of pre-sanction appraisal and post-sanction monitoring

unanswerable.question: What specific penalty clauses or financial liabilities must an NBFC include in third-party service provider agreements under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states NBFCs may incorporate terms to hold providers accountable but does not specify required penalty clauses, financial liability amounts, or mandatory contract provisions.

questions.question: What ongoing due diligence obligation does an NBFC have under the RBI's KYC Directions?
questions.answer: An NBFC must undertake ongoing due diligence of customers to ensure their transactions are consistent with the NBFC's knowledge about the customers, their business, risk profile, and source of funds or wealth.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall undertake ongoing due diligence of customers to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers' business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

questions.question: What customer information must an NBFC use as the basis for ongoing due diligence?
questions.answer: The NBFC must use its knowledge about the customer's business, risk profile, and source of funds or wealth to assess whether transactions are consistent.
questions.evidence: to ensure that their transactions are consistent with their knowledge about the customers, customers' business and risk profile, the source of funds / wealth.

unanswerable.question: What is the prescribed frequency for conducting ongoing due diligence reviews under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that NBFCs shall undertake ongoing due diligence but does not specify any frequency, timeline, or periodicity for such reviews.

questions.question: Who has the final authority to interpret the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Account Aggregator) Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: The Reserve Bank of India's interpretation of any provision of these Directions is final and binding.
questions.evidence: the interpretation of any provision of these Directions given by the RBI shall be final and binding

questions.question: Under what circumstances can the Reserve Bank of India issue clarifications on the NBFC Account Aggregator Directions?
questions.answer: The RBI may issue clarifications to give effect to the provisions or to remove difficulties in their application or interpretation, if it considers it necessary.
questions.evidence: For the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of these Directions or in order to remove any difficulties in the application or interpretation of the provisions of these Directions, the RBI may, if it considers necessary, issue necessary clarifications in respect of any matter covered herein

unanswerable.question: What is the time limit within which the RBI must respond to a clarification request submitted by an NBFC under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any timeline, deadline, or procedural requirement for the RBI to respond to clarification requests from NBFCs.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, who bears the responsibility for ensuring that the information reported to credit information companies is accurate and factually correct?
questions.answer: The reporting bank itself is responsible for the correctness of the information it reports and for ensuring the accuracy of all facts and figures submitted.
questions.evidence: The responsibility for reporting correct information and also ensuring the accuracy of facts and figures rests with the reporting bank.

questions.question: When a commercial bank submits data to credit information companies, what specific step must it take regarding the particulars of directors to verify their accuracy?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure the accuracy of directors' particulars and, wherever possible, cross-check them against the Registrar of Companies database.
questions.evidence: A bank, while furnishing information to credit information companies, shall ensure the accuracy of the particulars of the directors, and wherever possible, by cross-checking with the database maintained by the Registrar of Companies.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time limit allowed for a commercial bank to rectify inaccurate director particulars after they have been reported to a credit information company?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time limit, deadline, or rectification period for correcting reported information.

questions.question: What obligation does a commercial bank have regarding the process for identifying wilful defaulters under the RBI directions?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must establish a transparent mechanism covering the entire identification process to ensure penal provisions are applied fairly and discretion is eliminated.
questions.evidence: A bank shall put in place a transparent mechanism for the entire process of identification of wilful defaulters so that the penal provisions are applied in a fair manner and the scope for discretion is obviated.

questions.question: What is the intended outcome of the transparent mechanism that a commercial bank must implement for wilful defaulter identification?
questions.answer: The mechanism aims to ensure penal provisions are applied fairly and to remove any scope for discretion in the identification process.
questions.evidence: A bank shall put in place a transparent mechanism for the entire process of identification of wilful defaulters so that the penal provisions are applied in a fair manner and the scope for discretion is obviated.

unanswerable.question: Within what timeframe must a commercial bank implement the transparent mechanism for wilful defaulter identification after the directions come into force?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any implementation deadline or timeframe for establishing the transparent mechanism.

questions.question: How often must an NBFC review the risk categorisation of its customer accounts under the on-going due diligence requirements?
questions.answer: An NBFC must review risk categorisation at least once every six months.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall put in place a system of periodic review of risk categorisation of accounts, with such periodicity being at least once in every six months

questions.question: Which customer accounts does the rulebook single out for especially close transaction monitoring by an NBFC?
questions.answer: Accounts of marketing firms, particularly multi-level marketing (MLM) companies, must be closely monitored.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall closely monitor the transactions in accounts of marketing firms, especially accounts of Multi-level Marketing (MLM) companies.

unanswerable.question: What specific enhanced due diligence measures must an NBFC apply to high-risk accounts identified during the periodic review?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states the NBFC shall establish the need for enhanced due diligence measures but does not define what those measures are.

questions.question: Which customer groups must an NBFC's Customer Acceptance Policy avoid denying financial facilities to?
questions.answer: The policy must not deny facilities to the general public, particularly financially or socially disadvantaged individuals including Persons with Disabilities.
questions.evidence: The Customer Acceptance Policy shall not result in denial of a financial facility to members of the general public, especially those who are financially or socially disadvantaged, including the Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).

questions.question: What are the requirements for an NBFC when rejecting an application for onboarding or periodic KYC updation?
questions.answer: The NBFC must not reject such applications without applying its mind, and the concerned officer must record the reasons for rejection.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall not reject an application for onboarding or periodic updation of KYC without application of mind. The officer concerned shall duly record the reason(s) for rejection.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time allowed for the officer to record the reasons for rejection after an application is denied?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time limit or deadline for recording rejection reasons.

questions.question: What details must a commercial bank ensure are included in every communication sent by its recovery agents to a credit card holder?
questions.answer: Each communication must contain the name, email address, telephone number, and postal address of the senior officer at the card-issuing bank whom the customer can contact.
questions.evidence: All communications issued by recovery agents must contain the name, email-id, telephone number and address of the concerned senior officer of the card-issuer whom the customer can contact.

questions.question: When is a commercial bank required to share the recovery agent's name and contact details with the credit card holder?
questions.answer: The bank must provide this information immediately upon assigning the recovery agent to the cardholder's account.
questions.evidence: Further, card-issuers shall provide the name and contact details of the recovery agent to the cardholder immediately upon assigning the agent to the cardholder.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days a commercial bank has to notify the cardholder after assigning a recovery agent, and what penalty applies if this deadline is missed?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states the bank must act "immediately" but does not define a specific number of days or mention any penalty for delay.

questions.question: What written documentation must a commercial bank provide to a cardholder when issuing a credit or debit card?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must provide a set of contractual terms and conditions governing the issue and use of the card.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers shall make available to the cardholders in writing, a set of contractual terms and conditions governing the issue and use of such cards.

questions.question: What standards must the contractual terms between a commercial bank and a cardholder meet?
questions.answer: The terms must be expressed clearly and maintain a fair balance between the interests of both parties.
questions.evidence: These terms shall be expressed clearly and also maintain a fair balance between the interests of the parties concerned.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of card issuance must a commercial bank provide the written terms and conditions to the cardholder?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time limit or deadline for providing the terms and conditions to the cardholder.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a private sector bank, how far in advance must we submit a proposal for appointing a new MD&CEO to the RBI?
questions.answer: The proposal must be submitted at least four months before the expiry of the term of the present incumbent.
questions.evidence: A proposal for appointment of a new MD&CEO / CEO shall invariably contain a panel of at least two names in the order of preference and shall be submitted to RBI at least four months before the expiry of the term of office of the present incumbent.

questions.question: What forms and documents are required when seeking RBI's prior approval for the appointment or re-appointment of a Chairman or Whole Time Director or MD&CEO at a private sector bank?
questions.answer: Form B in Annex IV along with a Declaration and Undertaking from the candidate(s) and the remarks of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee confirming the information is true and complete.
questions.evidence: Appointment or re-appointment of Chairman or WTD or MD&CEO / CEO (by whatever name called) - Form ‘B’ in Annex IV along with ‘Declaration and Undertaking’ from candidate(s), and the remarks of NRC of having satisfied itself that the information is true and complete.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum permissible tenure for an MD&CEO at a private sector bank under these directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies submission timelines for appointment and re-appointment proposals but does not state any maximum tenure limit for an MD&CEO.

questions.question: Who has the final authority to interpret the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Digital Banking Channels Authorisation) Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: The Reserve Bank of India's interpretation of any provision is final and binding.
questions.evidence: the interpretation of any provision of these Directions given by the RBI shall be final and binding

questions.question: Can the Reserve Bank of India issue clarifications on matters covered by the Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: Yes, the RBI may issue necessary clarifications on any matter covered by the Directions if it considers it necessary.
questions.evidence: the RBI may, if it considers necessary, issue necessary clarifications in respect of any matter covered herein

unanswerable.question: What is the time limit within which the Reserve Bank of India must respond to a commercial bank's request for clarification on the Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states the RBI may issue clarifications but does not specify any timeline, deadline, or procedure for banks to request them or for the RBI to respond.

questions.question: Under what circumstances can a commercial bank increase the credit risk premium for an existing borrower?
questions.answer: A commercial bank may increase the credit risk premium for an existing borrower only if there is a deterioration in the borrower's credit risk profile or a change in the tenor premium.
questions.evidence: The credit risk premium charged to an existing borrower shall not be increased except on account of deterioration in the credit risk profile of the customer or change in tenor premium.

questions.question: Must the change in tenor premium be applied uniformly across all loan types for a given residual tenor under the Base Rate system?
questions.answer: Yes, the change in tenor premium on loans sanctioned under the Base Rate system must be uniform for all types of loans for a given residual tenor and cannot be borrower-specific or loan class-specific.
questions.evidence: The change in tenor premium on loans sanctioned under Base rate system shall not be borrower specific or loan class specific. In other words, the change in tenor premium shall be uniform for all types of loans for a given residual tenor.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum permissible percentage increase in the credit risk premium when a borrower's credit risk profile deteriorates?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the credit risk premium may be increased due to deterioration in credit risk profile but does not specify any cap, limit, or percentage on such an increase.

questions.question: Under the RBI's NBFC-AA Directions, 2025, what compliance obligation does an NBFC-Account Aggregator have regarding the Acquisition of Shareholding or Control Directions?
questions.answer: An NBFC-AA must comply with paragraphs 8 to 10 of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies– Acquisition of Shareholding or Control) Directions, 2025.
questions.evidence: NBFC-AA shall comply with the provisions of paragraphs 8 to 10 of Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies– Acquisition of Shareholding or Control) Directions, 2025.

questions.question: What topic does section G.3 of the NBFC-AA Directions address?
questions.answer: Section G.3 concerns the submission of information regarding changes to the NBFC-AA's address, directors, auditors, and similar details.
questions.evidence: G.3 Information with respect to change of address, directors, auditors, etc. to be submitted

unanswerable.question: What is the deadline for an NBFC-AA to submit the information required under section G.3?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only provides the heading for section G.3 and does not specify any time limit or deadline for submission.

questions.question: What is a commercial bank required to do with the details of third parties that played a vital role in credit sanction or disbursement and were negligent in a wilful default case?
questions.answer: The bank must forward those details to the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) for records, regardless of whether the bank is an IBA member.
questions.evidence: A bank shall forward the details of these third parties to the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) for records, regardless of the membership status of the bank with the IBA.

questions.question: What steps must a commercial bank take before it reports a third party to the IBA for involvement in a wilful default?
questions.answer: The bank must verify the third party's involvement and give the third party a chance to be heard, following a due process that is properly recorded.
questions.evidence: Before reporting to IBA, a bank shall satisfy itself of the involvement of concerned third parties and also provide them with an opportunity of being heard. In this regard, a bank shall follow due process, which shall be suitably recorded.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time allowed for a commercial bank to submit third-party details to the IBA after identifying their negligence in a wilful default?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any deadline or time limit for reporting third parties to the IBA.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, during which period each month is the minimum credit balance in a farmer's composite cash credit account measured for interest purposes?
questions.answer: The minimum credit balance is measured from the 10th day to the last day of each calendar month.
questions.evidence: during the period from the 10th to the last day of each calendar month

questions.question: What conditions must a commercial bank meet before paying interest on the minimum credit balance in a farmer's composite cash credit account?
questions.answer: The bank must comply with the conditions specified in paragraph 7 of the RBI Directions on Interest Rate on Deposits.
questions.evidence: subject to the conditions given in paragraph 7 of these Directions

unanswerable.question: What is the specific penalty amount or rate that a commercial bank must charge for premature withdrawal of a domestic term deposit under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only mentions the section heading 'J. Penalty on Premature Withdrawal of Domestic Term Deposit' but provides no details about penalty amounts, rates, or calculation methods.

questions.question: What documents must an NBFC provide to borrowers when sanctioning or disbursing a loan?
questions.answer: An NBFC must provide a copy of the loan agreement along with copies of all enclosures quoted in the loan agreement.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall invariably furnish a copy of the loan agreement along with a copy each of all enclosures quoted in the loan agreement to all the borrowers at the time of sanction / disbursement of loans

questions.question: At what stage must an NBFC furnish the loan agreement and enclosures to borrowers?
questions.answer: The NBFC must furnish these documents at the time of sanction or disbursement of loans.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall invariably furnish a copy of the loan agreement along with a copy each of all enclosures quoted in the loan agreement to all the borrowers at the time of sanction / disbursement of loans

unanswerable.question: What specific accommodations must an NBFC provide for loan facilities to physically or visually challenged borrowers?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only includes the heading 'A.9 Loan facilities to the physically / visually challenged' but provides no details or requirements for such facilities.

questions.question: How often must a commercial bank review its Base Rate under the RBI's 2025 Directions on Interest Rates on Advances?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must review its Base Rate at least once every quarter.
questions.evidence: A bank shall review the Base Rate at least once in a quarter

questions.question: Which governance bodies are authorized to approve the Base Rate review for a commercial bank under these Directions?
questions.answer: The review must be approved by either the Board or the Asset Liability Management Committee (ALCO), as per the bank's practice.
questions.evidence: with the approval of the Board or the Asset Liability Management Committees (ALCOs) as per the bank's practice

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days after quarter-end by which a commercial bank must complete its Base Rate review?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies the review frequency (at least once a quarter) and the approving authorities, but does not state any deadline or time limit for completing the review after the quarter ends.

questions.question: How frequently must an NBFC verify the UNSCR 1718 Sanctions List for updates?
questions.answer: An NBFC must verify the list every day to capture any additions, deletions, or other changes.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall verify every day, the 'UNSCR 1718 Sanctions List of Designated Individuals and Entities'

questions.question: Which specific sanctions list is an NBFC required to check daily under the KYC Directions?
questions.answer: The NBFC is required to check the UNSCR 1718 Sanctions List of Designated Individuals and Entities.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall verify every day, the 'UNSCR 1718 Sanctions List of Designated Individuals and Entities'

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time allowed for an NBFC to freeze the assets of a person newly added to the UNSCR 1718 list?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph mandates daily verification of the list but does not specify any deadline or time limit for taking freezing action after a new designation appears.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank consider regarding customer suitability when introducing a new housing finance product?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must take into account customer suitability and appropriateness when introducing any product.
questions.evidence: the bank while introducing any kind of product shall take into account the customer suitability and appropriateness

questions.question: What disclosure must a commercial bank make to borrowers when launching a new housing finance product?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure borrowers are made fully aware of the risks and liabilities associated with the product.
questions.evidence: ensure that the borrowers / customers are made fully aware of the risks and liabilities under such products

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of product launch must a commercial bank provide the risk disclosure documentation to borrowers?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any timeline or deadline for providing risk disclosures to borrowers.

questions.question: Which other Reserve Bank of India directions on income recognition, asset classification and provisioning apply to an NBFC-MFI?
questions.answer: The Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025 apply to NBFC-MFIs, except where they contradict the NBFC-MFI Directions.
questions.evidence: All other provisions contained in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025, where not contradictory to the contents of these directions, shall be applicable to NBFC-MFIs.

questions.question: Can an NBFC-MFI ignore a provision in the 2025 Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning Directions if it conflicts with the NBFC-MFI Directions?
questions.answer: Yes, provisions in the 2025 IRACP Directions that contradict the NBFC-MFI Directions do not apply to NBFC-MFIs.
questions.evidence: All other provisions contained in Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025, where not contradictory to the contents of these directions, shall be applicable to NBFC-MFIs.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific provisioning requirement for standard assets held by an NBFC-MFI under these directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only states that the 2025 IRACP Directions apply where not contradictory; it does not specify any provisioning percentages, asset classification thresholds, or numeric requirements for standard or non-performing assets.

questions.question: How often must an NBFC check the UN sanctions lists and the domestic terrorism schedules for updates?
questions.answer: An NBFC must verify the UNSC sanctions lists and the schedules to the 2007 Order on a daily basis and incorporate any additions, deletions, or changes immediately.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall verify the aforementioned lists, i.e., UNSC Sanctions Lists and lists as available in the Schedules to the Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism (Implementation of Security Council Resolutions) Order, 2007, as amended from time to time, on a daily basis, and any modifications to the lists in terms of additions, deletions or other changes shall be taken into account by the NBFC for meticulous compliance.

questions.question: What must an NBFC do if it finds an account matching a name on the UN or domestic terrorist lists?
questions.answer: The NBFC must report the account details to FIU-IND and advise the Ministry of Home Affairs, and strictly follow the freezing procedure laid down in the UAPA Order dated February 2, 2021.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall report the details of accounts resembling any of the individuals / entities in the lists to FIU-IND in addition to advising the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) as required under UAPA notification dated February 2, 2021 ( Annex I of these Directions).

unanswerable.question: Within how many hours of identifying a match must an NBFC freeze the assets of a listed individual or entity?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that the NBFC shall follow the procedure in the UAPA Order dated February 2, 2021, but does not specify any time limit or deadline for freezing assets.
